message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most famous American composers—both classical and popular—whose work has had a lasting impact on music worldwide:

| Composer | Era / Genre | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | Jazz‑Classical crossover | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | Classical, film scores | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man*, *Elmer Gantry* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | Broadway, symphonic | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *On the Town* |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film composer | *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park* |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*, *Koyaanisqatsi* |
| **Ludwig van Beethoven** (1770–1827) | Classical | *Symphony No. 9*, *Moonlight Sonata* |
| **Claude Debussy** (1862–1918) | Impressionism | *Clair de Lune*, *Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun* |
| **Igor Stravinsky** (1882–1971) | Modernist | *The Firebird*, *The Rite of Spring* |
| **Béla Bartók** (1881–1945) | Folk‑inspired modernism | *Concerto for Orchestra*, *Music for Strings, Percussion, and Celesta* |
| **Duke Ellington** (1899–1974) | Jazz | *Mood Indigo*, *Take the A Train*, *Satin Doll* |
| **Miles Davis** (1926–1991) | Jazz | *Kind of Blue*, *Bitches Brew*, *Sketches of Spain* |
| **Bob Dylan** (born 1941) | Folk/rock | *Blowin’ in the Wind*, *Like a Rolling Stone*, *The Times They Are a-Changin’* |
| **John Lennon** (1940–1980) | Rock | *Imagine*, *Hey Jude*, *Let It Be* |
| **Paul McCartney** (born 1942) | Rock | *Yesterday*, *Let It Be*, *Live and Let Die* |
| **David Bowie** (1947–2016) | Rock | *Space Oddity*, *Heroes*, *Ziggy Stardust* |
| **Prince** (1958–2016) | Pop/R&B | *Purple Rain*, *When Doves Cry*, *1999* |
| **Taylor Swift** (born 1989) | Country/pop | *Love Story*, *Shake It Off*, *Blank Space* |

These artists span a wide range of styles—from early 20th‑century classical and jazz to contemporary pop—and each has left an indelible mark on both American and global music culture.
